title: A Cunard liner torpedoed on its way home to Liverpool
spotify: Witness History Sinking of the Lusitania
description: On 7 May 1915 a German U-boat sank the Cunard liner Lusitania off Ireland as it sailed from New York to Liverpool; about 1,200 died. Witness History draws on archive survivor accounts. Cunard’s old headquarters, the Cunard Building, stands at Pier Head.

title: Wartime sailors deported, families left behind
episode: The scandal of Liverpool's missing Chinese sailors
spotify: Witness History The scandal of Liverpool's missing Chinese sailors
description: Thousands of Chinese seamen kept supplies reaching Liverpool in the Second World War. After 1945 the British authorities forced many out, leaving wives and children behind. Many sailed for the Blue Funnel Line, based at India Buildings on Water Street.

title: The first intercity railway nearly dies in Parliament
episode: Liverpool & Manchester Railway pt. 1 - The Fight for the Idea
spotify: History of the Railways Liverpool & Manchester Railway pt. 1 - The Fight for the Idea
description: The Liverpool and Manchester Railway of 1830 was the first intercity line worked only by steam, yet engineer George Stephenson nearly sank it in Parliament. Its Liverpool end climbed to Edge Hill, where the 1836 station still takes passengers.

title: A concrete tent under a stained-glass crown
episode: S2 E07 • The Art of Liverpool's Catholic Cathedral
place: Metropolitan Cathedral of Christ the King
spotify: Exhibiting Faith S2 E07 • The Art of Liverpool's Catholic Cathedral
description: Writer David Trigg and Laura Moffatt of Art + Christianity tour the art of the Metropolitan Cathedral of Christ the King, England’s largest Catholic cathedral, a circular 1967 church under John Piper’s glass lantern, with former organist Terry Duffy.

title: Britain’s biggest cathedral, raised over an old quarry
episode: O Come All Ye Faithful: The story of the UK's largest cathedral
spotify: Uncharted Liverpool O Come All Ye Faithful: The story of the UK's largest cathedral
description: Uncharted Liverpool on the Anglican Liverpool Cathedral: why it was built on St James’s Mount, above a former quarry turned cemetery, who designed it, and the odd details inside. Begun in 1904 and finished in 1978, it is Britain’s largest cathedral.

title: The women who worked the sugar refinery on Love Lane
episode: Meet the Sugar Girls of Love Lane. New social history book set in Tate & Lyle's Liverpool factory in the sixties offers a glimpse of a long vanished era.
place: Tate & Lyle refinery site, Love Lane
spotify: From the Library With Love Meet the Sugar Girls of Love Lane. New social history book set in Tate & Lyle's Liverpool factory in the sixties offers a glimpse of a long vanished era.
description: Authors Duncan Barrett and Nuala Calvi on The Sugar Girls of Love Lane, their book of stories from women who worked at Tate & Lyle’s sugar refinery on Love Lane, in the dockside Vauxhall district, in the 1960s. The refinery closed in 1981.

title: Bombs, rumours and the government’s morale reports
episode: Morale, morality and the Liverpool Blitz
place: St Luke’s bombed-out church, Leece Street
spotify: The National Archives Podcast Series Morale, morality and the Liverpool Blitz
description: A talk from The National Archives on how the wartime government measured the morale of Liverpudlians during the Blitz, some of the heaviest bombing in Britain. St Luke’s Church, burned out in May 1941, stands roofless on Leece Street as a memorial.

title: How a port city came to talk Scouse
description: Linguist Tony Crowley, who grew up in central Liverpool, on Scouse, the city’s accent and dialect, named after lobscouse, a sailors’ stew. Scotland Road, the old Irish working-class district north of the centre, is where much of that mix of voices settled.

title: A seventieth birthday on the Mersey ferry
episode: Edwina Currie: A Ferry Across the Mersey
spotify: The Essay Edwina Currie: A Ferry Across the Mersey
description: Liverpool-born politician and novelist Edwina Currie, who turned 70 the same year as BBC Radio 3, marks its birthday with an essay on the ferry across the River Mersey, which sails from the Pier Head terminal.

title: A church fête, a skiffle band and a boy with a guitar
spotify: The Retrospectors When Lennon Met McCartney
description: On 6 July 1957 John Lennon’s skiffle group the Quarrymen played the summer fête at St Peter’s Church in Woolton, a south Liverpool suburb. That afternoon a friend introduced him to 15-year-old Paul McCartney. The Retrospectors tell the story.

title: A radical city and its fight with Westminster
spotify: Explaining History A radical history of Liverpool
description: Historian David Swift, author of Scouse Republic, on Liverpool’s radical politics and its 1980s decline, when the Labour council, run from the Municipal Buildings on Dale Street, defied Margaret Thatcher’s government over its budget.

title: Thirty years of digging, and no reason given
place: Williamson Tunnels Heritage Centre, Smithdown Lane
spotify: Jimmy Akin's Mysterious World Joseph Williamson’s Tunnels
description: Tobacco merchant Joseph Williamson paid men for about 30 years to dig tunnels under his Edge Hill estate and never said why. Jimmy Akin and Dom Bettinelli weigh seven theories. Part of the maze is open at the Williamson Tunnels Heritage Centre.
